Data Sources & References

Comprehensive APA 7th Edition Citations for the General Social Survey (GSS) and Methodology

1. Primary Empirical Data Source

The empirical analysis in this project is based on data from the General Social Survey (GSS), conducted by NORC at the University of Chicago.

General Social Survey (NORC at the University of Chicago)

  • Reference List Citation: > Davern, M., Bautista, R., Freese, J., Herd, P., & Morgan, S. L. (2024). General Social Survey 1972–2024 (Release 3) [Data set]. NORC at the University of Chicago. https://gssdataexplorer.norc.org

  • In-Text Citation: > (Davern et al., 2024)

  • Dataset Scope & Methodology: The General Social Survey (GSS) is one of the nation’s most authoritative, long-running social science research studies. Since 1972, the GSS has monitored societal trends and demographic transformations across the adult, non-institutionalized population of the United States using nationally representative probability sampling.

2. Variable Codebook & Descriptions

Below are the official GSS codebook definitions for all 15 variables analyzed in this study:

Variable Name GSS Label Description & Coding Scheme
educ Respondent Educational Attainment Highest grade of school completed (0–20 years). Recoded into 4 tiers: High School or Less, Some College, Bachelor Degree, Graduate Degree.
paeduc Father’s Educational Attainment Highest grade of school completed by respondent’s father (0–20 years).
maeduc Mother’s Educational Attainment Highest grade of school completed by respondent’s mother (0–20 years).
incom16 Relative Family Income at Age 16 Family income at age 16 relative to American families: 1 = Far Below Average, 2 = Below Average, 3 = Average, 4 = Above Average, 5 = Far Above Average.
family16 Family Structure at Age 16 Living arrangement at age 16: Both Own Parents, Single Parent, Stepparent, Other Relative/Arrangement.
res16 Residence Type at Age 16 Type of place lived in at age 16: Farm, Country Non-Farm, Town <50k, 50k to 250k, Big-City Suburb, City >250k.
sex Respondent’s Sex Sex assigned at interview: Female, Male.
race Respondent’s Race Race of respondent: White, Black, Other.
born Respondent Born in U.S. Was the respondent born in the United States? Yes, No.
parborn Parents Born in U.S. Were respondent’s parents born in the U.S.? Both U.S., One U.S., Neither U.S.
sibs Number of Siblings Total number of brothers and sisters (0 to 6+).
childs Number of Children Ever had children / total number of children (0 to 8+).
age Respondent’s Age Age at time of interview (18 to 89 years).
year Survey Administration Year Calendar year of survey round (1972 through 2024).
agekdbrn Age at First Child’s Birth Age when respondent’s first child was born. (Excluded from final predictive model due to 62.1% missingness/inapplicability across historical survey rounds).
